project_type: Docker image build repo (thin layer over nousresearch/hermes-agent) with Renovate self-hosted via GitHub Actions. No application code: the deliverables are a Dockerfile, renovate.json, GitHub workflows, and docs.
language: Dockerfile + YAML + JSON. New helper script must be Node.js ESM (node stdlib only, no npm deps) because it has to run inside the ghcr.io/renovatebot/renovate container, which ships Node but does not guarantee jq/curl.
build_system: docker build (BuildKit via docker/build-push-action in CI, plain `docker build` locally). Single platform linux/amd64 only (audit finding P-03). No make, no package.json, no lockfile.
test_framework: No unit test framework. Verification = (1) `docker build`, (2) the smoke test in .github/workflows/pr-validation.yml which runs `docker run --entrypoint <tool>` for the 5 tools, (3) entrypoint+arch assertions via `docker image inspect`, (4) two Trivy scans (informative report + blocking gate on new fixable CRITICALs filtered by .trivyignore), (5) `renovate-config-validator` for renovate.json.
build_command: docker build -t hermes-leo-custom:local .   (from /projects/sandbox/hermes-leo-config). Note: the Go layer downloads ~300 MB, a cold build takes several minutes.
test_command: Replicate pr-validation.yml locally: docker build -t hermes-leo-custom:local . && for the 5 tools: docker run --rm --entrypoint gws hermes-leo-custom:local --version ; --entrypoint gh ... --version ; --entrypoint kubectl ... version --client ; --entrypoint devin ... --version ; --entrypoint go ... version. Then: docker image inspect --format '{{json .Config.Entrypoint}}' must equal ["/opt/hermes/docker/entrypoint-dispatch.sh"] and --format '{{.Architecture}}' must equal amd64. Renovate config: npx --yes --package renovate@44.61.6 renovate-config-validator renovate.json
verification_instructions: 1) `npx --yes --package renovate@44.61.6 renovate-config-validator renovate.json` must report 'Config validated successfully' with no ERROR lines (44.61.6 is the Renovate version this repo actually runs, per PR #26 metadata). 2) Run the new checksum script in --check mode against unmodified main: all 5 tools must report OK (all 5 committed checksums were confirmed correct by the architect, see key_patterns). 3) Simulate PR #26: set ARG GO_VERSION=1.27.1 in the Dockerfile, run the script with --write, and assert GO_SHA256 becomes 63d339f0da5ab53635a56f2490a7984dfe12dfcff22ad749f63edaf590168445 and that the other four SHA256 ARGs are byte-identical to before. 4) `docker build` that simulated state to green, then run the 5 smoke commands and the entrypoint/arch assertions. 5) Revert the simulated bump so the committed Dockerfile stays at GO_VERSION=1.27.0 unless the feature says otherwise.
snapshot_or_generated_files: The five ARG <TOOL>_SHA256 lines in the Dockerfile are effectively generated/checked-in data. After this task they are regenerated by the new script (`--write`) and validated in CI (`--check`). There are no other generated or snapshot files.

environment_constraints: Network is OPEN and verified reachable for every upstream needed: go.dev, github.com, api.github.com, dl.k8s.io, static.devin.ai, registry.npmjs.org, and the Docker registry. `docker build` works locally. `gh api` (REST) works read-only; GraphQL-backed `gh pr` / `gh issue` subcommands FAIL in this environment, so always use `gh api repos/rjullien/hermes-leo-config/...`. contribution_requirements: From AGENTS.md (mandatory): NEVER commit a secret (public repo). Do not change the FROM base image. gws must stay the glibc `-unknown-linux-gnu` build, not musl. Every pinned version ARG must keep its preceding `# renovate: datasource=... depName=...` comment. Do not disable Renovate automerge and do not reintroduce RENOVATE_AUTOMERGE=false in renovate.yml. Commits follow Conventional Commits (feat/fix/ci/chore/docs). Any behaviour change must be reflected in README.md, and AGENTS.md rule 5 must be updated since it currently documents only the version ARG convention and not the machine-maintained SHA256 ARG.
key_patterns: Dockerfile layer layout (P-02): for each of the 5 tools, a `# renovate:` comment, then `ARG <TOOL>_VERSION=`, then `ARG <TOOL>_SHA256=`, then the RUN that curls into /tmp, verifies with `echo "${<TOOL>_SHA256}  /tmp/x" | sha256sum -c -`, and only then extracts. Order is gws (L36-42) -> gh (L45-53) -> kubectl (L56-61) -> devin (L64-75) -> go (L78-92); do not reorder, the order is deliberate cache optimisation. UPSTREAM CHECKSUM SOURCES, ALL FIVE VERIFIED BY EXECUTION AGAINST THE CURRENTLY COMMITTED VALUES: gws -> https://github.com/googleworkspace/cli/releases/download/v<V>/google-workspace-cli-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz.sha256 (0.22.5 -> de78ecdbd2f1a84cca0063a7ecbc440240fc14b6ebccbb17f4646b792a8c5c1f, matches); gh -> https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/download/v<V>/gh_<V>_checksums.txt, take the line ending in gh_<V>_linux_amd64.tar.gz (2.99.0 -> ed4960225d2833e04a61590d9fa2b5773d147f3aa375459e5466a40c102f3832, matches); kubectl -> https://dl.k8s.io/release/v<V>/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl.sha256, bare hex, checksum of the raw binary not a tarball (1.37.0 -> 6129359f4e1f3848a5572ccb0b26cf28b8ca08cef38c95a765b2f64a2c961a2f, matches); devin -> https://static.devin.ai/cli/<V>/manifest.json, field .platforms["x86_64-unknown-linux"].sha256 (3000.6.7 -> f88edacea692553910d72f275515bd0b52b5d271d55250981b0c41011142d27b, matches); go -> https://go.dev/dl/?mode=json&include=all, select the entry with .version=="go<V>" then the file with os==linux, arch==amd64, kind==archive, field .sha256 (go1.27.0 -> 675c26c449cbb18fc24b74650de1eabbae6e16f64326fd85a283fb3b58280685, matches; go1.27.1 -> 63d339f0da5ab53635a56f2490a7984dfe12dfcff22ad749f63edaf590168445). CRITICAL CORRECTION: go.dev does NOT publish a per-tarball .sha256 file. https://go.dev/dl/go1.27.1.linux-amd64.tar.gz.sha256 returns an HTML page, not a hash. Any implementation that assumes that URL will silently write HTML garbage. Use the ?mode=json endpoint.

problem_statement: The Dockerfile pins version and checksum as two independent ARGs. Renovate only knows the version ARG, bumps it, and leaves the SHA256 stale, so `sha256sum -c` correctly rejects the new artifact and the build fails. This is structural and affects all 5 tools. Confirmed live symptoms from Dependency Dashboard issue #4 and PR #26: (a) PR #26 golang 1.27.1 is mergeable_state=blocked because its build fails at 'Build image (no push)'; (b) branch renovate/kubernetes-kubernetes-digest is Errored trying to 'update kubernetes/kubernetes digest to f54c212', i.e. Renovate wants to write a GIT COMMIT SHA of the kubernetes/kubernetes repo into KUBECTL_SHA256, which would be a wrong value even if it landed; (c) Renovate reports 'Could not determine new digest for update (github-releases package googleworkspace/cli)', the same for cli/cli, and 'Failed to look up custom package devin-cli: no-result', which means gws, gh and devin are receiving NO updates at all and have been silently frozen since the customManager was introduced. All four symptoms trace back to the single `(?<currentDigest>[a-f0-9]{64})` capture group in renovate.json: none of the datasources in use (golang-version, github-releases, github-tags, custom) can supply a tarball SHA-256 as a digest, so Renovate either errors, substitutes an unrelated git SHA, or abandons the lookup.
chosen_approach: Option 2 as chosen by the user, hardened. (1) Remove the currentDigest capture group from the customManager so Renovate goes back to plain version-only bumps for all 5 tools, which alone unfreezes gws/gh/devin and stops the bogus kubectl digest update. (2) Add a committed, dependency-free Node script scripts/sync-download-checksums.mjs that resolves the upstream published checksum for a tool, independently downloads the artifact and recomputes its SHA-256, refuses to emit a value unless the two agree, and then writes the ARG. Two agreeing sources is what preserves audit finding S-01: the value committed in the repo is still an independently attested expectation, not something taken on trust at build time. (3) Wire it into Renovate via postUpgradeTasks so the corrected checksum is part of the Renovate commit and stays reviewable in the diff. (4) Add a fast --check job in pr-validation.yml so that if postUpgradeTasks ever fails to run, the PR fails early with an explicit checksum-mismatch message instead of an opaque sha256sum error buried in a 300 MB build. Rejected alternative: resolving the checksum at build time by curling the .sha256 (this was option 3, rejected because the repo would no longer commit an independently reviewed expected value, gutting S-01).
